answer: Women's Health - 340B savings support affordable access to long-acting reversible contraception, including IUDs and Nexplanon, while strengthening Care Alliance's capacity to deliver comprehensive women's health services. Revenue generated through the program helps sustain clinical staffing, care coordination, patient education, and operational infrastructure that expands access for uninsured, underserved, and vulnerable populations.

Substance Use Disorder Management - 340B pricing expands access to medications for opioid use disorder, including Sublocade, Vivitrol, and buprenorphine/naloxone (Suboxone). Program savings support integrated behavioral health services, recovery resources, clinical staffing, and operational infrastructure, strengthening Care Alliance's ability to serve individuals experiencing homelessness, substance use disorders, and other complex social need

HIV Prevention - 340B savings increase access to HIV prevention through PrEP medications, including Truvada, Descovy, and Apretude. Revenue supports patient navigation, laboratory monitoring, medication adherence, insurance assistance, outreach, and the operational infrastructure needed to expand preventive services for uninsured, underserved, and high-risk populations.

HIV Treatment - 340B pricing supports access to life-saving antiretroviral therapy, including Cabenuva, Biktarvy, and Genvoya, while strengthening comprehensive HIV care. Program savings are reinvested into pharmacy services, multidisciplinary care coordination, clinical staffing, outreach, and operational infrastructure, helping sustain services for people living with HIV, including those who are uninsured, experiencing homelessness, or otherwise medically underserved.

The 340B Drug Pricing Program plays an important role in supporting Care Alliance Health Center's clinical operations and financial sustainability. Savings generated through the program are reinvested to support patient care, pharmacy operations, clinical staffing, care coordination, community outreach, and other organizational functions that improve access to comprehensive healthcare services for medically underserved populations.

Care Alliance provides integrated primary care, behavioral health, pharmacy, women's health, infectious disease, and substance use disorder services across multiple clinical and community-based settings. The organization serves patients residing in public housing, individuals receiving substance use treatment, people experiencing homelessness through men's and women's shelters, school-based populations, and other underserved communities throughout Northeast Ohio. 340B savings help offset the cost of providing care to uninsured and underinsured patients while supporting access to high-cost medications for HIV treatment and prevention, opioid use disorder, women's health, and other chronic conditions.

As the healthcare landscape continues to evolve, Care Alliance anticipates an increased reliance on 340B program savings to help maintain organizational stability and preserve access to care. Medicaid work requirements and other policy changes may increase the number of patients experiencing interruptions in insurance coverage or financial barriers to obtaining medications. Continued reinvestment of 340B savings allows the organization to sustain essential clinical services, maintain operational capacity, and ensure vulnerable populations continue to receive coordinated, high-quality care regardless of their ability to pay.
